cut_items.item: Run git fetch and git log HEAD..origin/<branch> before pushing to see whether someone else pushed commits you don't recognize
Check that the branch is yours alone before force-pushing; force-pushing will break teammates' local copies
Protected branches will usually reject force pushes anyway
An open PR updates automatically after the force push
Reviewers may need to re-review, and line comments can lose their anchors after a rebase

added_items.item: If --force-with-lease is rejected, run git fetch and check git log origin/<branch> for commits you don't have, then rebase onto them or confirm they are safe to drop before retrying
Commits that exist only on the remote are lost by a force push
Teammates must rebase or reset their copies after a force push
Recovery steps if --force-with-lease is rejected: fetch, inspect git log origin/<branch>, rebase onto the new commits or confirm they can be dropped, then retry
Explicit warning that commits existing only on the remote are lost after a force push
